scope: Local database-failure chaos state, fail-closed health/readiness, durable HTTP mutation containment, production-like chaos guard and operational contracts

criteria.description: An initialized database runtime under database-failure exposes unavailable persistence and does not fall back to in-memory persistence.
criteria.limitations: This proves the local chaos projection only; it does not prove a real database outage, failover or target recovery behavior.

criteria.description: Health/readiness/liveness preserve their transport contracts while reporting unavailable persistence and closing readiness.
criteria.limitations: The compact /health transport remains 200 with ok=false when degraded; /ready and /health/ready are the admission gates and /live is liveness-only.

criteria.description: Authenticated tenant mutations and public durable webhook mutations are rejected with a stable 503 before durable handlers can acknowledge work during database-failure.
criteria.limitations: The local HTTP proof covers bearer-authenticated application mutation, synthetic PIX and WhatsApp inbound. API-key mutation during the active chaos window is not separately exercised.

criteria.description: Production-like HTTP start/stop chaos mutations are disabled before experiment execution, while authenticated listing remains read-only.
criteria.limitations: The proof uses local production-like configuration and does not authorize or exercise target production operations.

criteria.description: Metrics, OpenAPI, alerts, experiment description and runbooks consistently describe unavailable persistence and fail-closed recovery.
criteria.limitations: Static and local contract evidence does not replace a target alert delivery or game-day execution.

criteria.description: TDD, API regression, workspace regression, coverage, build, lint, typecheck, security and static quality rails pass locally.
criteria.limitations: Remote CI, target operations, real providers, production and release acceptance remain unverified.

review.summary: Independent read-only review found no Critical or High issue after the write guard, contract and documentation remediation; the review remains conditional and is not production approval.

conditions: Keep database-failure fail-closed: do not acknowledge clinical, financial or durable webhook mutations while persistence is unavailable.
Keep in-memory mode limited to explicit local bootstrap without a configured database; do not interpret it as outage recovery.
Obtain separate authority before real database failure injection, target operations, provider credentials, deployment, recovery automation or release acceptance.
Close the global Vetus, clinical, enterprise-readiness, target, operational and release gates separately; this slice does not promote them.
non_claims: No real database outage, failover, backup/restore, RTO/RPO or automated recovery evidence
No target role/RLS, managed Redis, provider, staging, production, remote CI or release evidence
No global parity or enterprise-readiness approval
